question: _______, (born c. 350 BC-died c. 290), ancient Greek historian and diplomat, is author of Indica.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Megasthenes**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Megasthenes was an ancient Greek historian and diplomat who is best known for his work *Indica*, which provided an account of India and its people based on his observations during his time as an ambassador in the Maurya Empire.
 
• Megasthenes (c. 350 BC - c. 290 BC) was a Greek historian and diplomat who served as an ambassador to the Maurya Empire during the reign of Emperor Chandragupta Maurya (the founder of the Maurya dynasty).
 
• He was sent to India by Seleucus I, one of Alexander the Great's generals who later founded the Seleucid Empire.
 
• Megasthenes is most famous for his work *Indica*, which he wrote based on his experiences and observations during his stay at the Mauryan court in Pataliputra (modern-day Patna).
 
• In *Indica*, he described various aspects of Indian society, culture, geography, and the political system under Chandragupta Maurya.
 
• While his account was not purely historical, it provided valuable insights into the life of ancient India and was an important source for later Greek historians.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• **Xuanzang**: A Chinese Buddhist monk who traveled to India in the 7th century and wrote a detailed account of his journey, but lived centuries after Megasthenes.
 
• **James Legge**: A Scottish sinologist and missionary, primarily known for his translations of Chinese texts, not involved with India.
 
• **Seleucus I**: A Greek general and founder of the Seleucid Empire who sent Megasthenes as an ambassador to India, but did not write *Indica*.
